answer: An agent economy can throttle Sybil attacks by pricing identity with a one-way burn. Each agent locks a modest ember of value into a commitment bound to its key; that cost is unrecoverable, so influence tracks destroyed stake rather than the size of the lagoon of wallets one controls. A newcomer may still join at dawn with an equal voice, but an attacker who wants a voting majority must burn more than every honest agent combined. Cloning names adds no votes and only drains the same fixed budget, making the takeover prohibitively expensive.
